brief.summary: Set 12-month priorities around one governed workflow, not tool sprawl. At maturity 2 (single pilot), the 12 MSLs and 3 medical information specialists should (1) formalize the existing pilot as an evidence-grounding and literature-triage workflow, with MSLs using PubMed plus an AI layer to summarize and triangulate literature before HCP conversations, and medical information using the same grounded corpus for response drafting; (2) build a risk-based human-oversight and auditability standard for AI-assisted content, mapped to FDA's January 2025 SIUU guidance, so AI-drafted answers stay inside scientific-exchange boundaries; (3) instrument the workflow in Veeva CRM, using voice-note-to-insight capture and insight tagging so field intelligence feeds a single insight backlog; (4) upskill the team on data literacy and prompt/verification discipline, since benchmark work shows the shift from content creation to analytics and the need for upskilling; and (5) define a small set of maturity metrics (time-to-answer, citation accuracy, insight-to-action rate) before expanding to a second workflow. Keep Excel for tracking and measurement only; avoid new platforms until the pilot shows measura

debate.name: Dr. Priya Raman
debate.statement: Marcus is right that the pilot must show where MSL hours move, and that is exactly why the two steps belong in one governed workflow rather than two. If triage and drafting share one grounded corpus and one audit path, the hours returned and the hours spent verifying are both vis

debate.name: Marcus Feld
debate.statement: I accept the single governed path if the measurement is built in from day one. My condition stands: baseline where MSL hours sit today before the pilot starts, so returned triage time is shown moving into verification and conversation prep, not just disappearing into a dashboard.

debate.name: Elena Voss
debate.statement: Tomas is correct that oversight labor is the hidden cost, and risk-based review tiers are the cheaper control than uniform review. But tiers only save money if the oversight hours are budgeted explicitly, so the pilot should cost the reviewer time per tier, not assume it away.

debate.name: Tomas Berg
debate.statement: Sofia's point that drafting tolerates less drift than triage supports tiering rather than contradicting it. The response side gets the stricter verification tier and the oversight record is the defensible artifact, so the review standard is defined before volume grows, not after.

debate.name: Sofia Lindqvist
debate.statement: Amara is right that citation accuracy on drafted answers must be tested against a fixed sample before expansion. The three of us already know where drafting drifts, so the pilot should encode that into the verification tier and the prompt discipline rather than discover it at sca

debate.name: Nadia Okafor
debate.statement: Omar is right that the audit trail belongs in Veeva CRM fields and Excel logs, not side documents. At maturity 2 the technology work is making the single pilot record what was asked, what PubMed evidence was retrieved, and where the human overrode, inside the system of record we

debate.name: Dr. Leo Marchetti
debate.statement: One governed workflow is fine, but the MSLs will treat AI output as a shortcut unless summarization is visibly separated from verified evidence. The pilot must ring-fence the returned triage time for citation checking and conversation prep, or the workflow just adds steps without

debate.name: Grace Chen
debate.statement: Elena's point about hidden oversight cost is the procurement case for proving the workflow before buying anything. The purchasing gate should be measurable time-to-answer, citation accuracy, and audit completeness on the existing stack, so no AI layer is bought until the pilot cl

debate.name: Dr. Samuel Adeyemi
debate.statement: Nadia has the right system of record, but the lineage must cover both literature summaries and drafted answers, recording which PubMed sources were retrieved, which version was used, and where a human verified or overrode. That is a data-lineage requirement before it is a review

debate.name: Dr. Hana Sato
debate.statement: Leo's separation of summarization from verified evidence matches what HCPs will do to MSLs: test them on provenance and nuance. The workflow should make it normal for an MSL to say what was AI-assisted, what was verified, and where the evidence is thin, so the summary prepares th

debate.name: Dr. Amara Diallo
debate.statement: Sofia is right that the three specialists already know where drafting drifts, so let us encode that now. My fixed sample of drafted answers gets scored on citation accuracy before any volume expansion, and the stricter response-side tier is the gate, not an afterthought.

debate.name: Ravi Menon
debate.statement: Marcus's baseline condition is the whole value case. Before the pilot starts we log where MSL hours sit today in Excel, so returned triage time can be shown moving into verification and conversation prep rather than vanishing into a dashboard nobody audits.

debate.name: Claire Dubois
debate.statement: Hana's point about evidence being thin is exactly where HEOR conversations break. The grounding workflow should flag indirect and gap-heavy evidence explicitly rather than smooth it, so an MSL can say plainly where the literature does not carry the claim.

debate.name: Kenji Watanabe
debate.statement: Mei-Lin is right that verification must be a trained habit, and at maturity 2 skill is the binding constraint. A shared checklist and peer review in the first weeks is the training artifact, but it only holds if the checklist is the same one the audit record cites.

debate.name: Dr. Fiona Blake
debate.statement: Nadia's audit trail records what was asked and retrieved, but insight capture dies if tagged insights never land anywhere with an owner. The pilot needs one backlog with a disposition field, or the field intelligence the workflow generates converts to nothing.

debate.name: Dr. Yusuf Karim
debate.statement: Samuel's lineage requirement starts upstream of the record: retrieval itself must be reproducible. At maturity 2 the MSLs need one documented PubMed triage protocol so every summary traces to a search someone else could rerun, not an ad hoc query.

debate.name: Beatriz Almeida
debate.statement: Claire's gap-flagging matters most on the payer side, where indirect and comparative evidence is what gets flattened. The corpus should mark where comparative claims rest on indirect data so MSLs do not overstate support in front of payer audiences.

debate.name: Dr. Ingrid Solberg
debate.statement: Tomas's tiers cover scientific drift but not the safety boundary. A drafted answer can be citation-accurate and still cross into safety signal territory, so the oversight standard needs an explicit trigger for when a response goes to safety review instead of routine scientific re

debate.name: Omar Haddad
debate.statement: Samuel is right that lineage comes first, and it has to be enforceable, which means the retrieval, version, and override fields live in Veeva CRM and the Excel log, not side documents. If the record sits outside the system of record, the oversight standard is unenforceable.

debate.name: Dr. Mei-Lin Chow
debate.statement: Kenji and I agree the constraint is skill, so the pilot trains verification as a habit from week one: each MSL paired with a checklist and a peer reviewer. Policy alone will not change behavior in twelve people carrying a full load.

debate.name: Dr. Priya Raman
debate.statement: Marcus, I accept your baseline condition as part of the governed workflow itself, not a side exercise. The first thing we do is log current MSL hours in Excel, then run the single triage-and-drafting path so returned time is visibly redeployed into verification and conversation p

debate.name: Marcus Feld
debate.statement: Ravi has made the baseline concrete, so let us lock it before any pilot activity: hours logged in Excel by task, reviewed weekly. The pilot's success test is where those hours move, and if they do not move into verification and conversation prep, we stop and redesign.

debate.name: Elena Voss
debate.statement: Grace's purchasing gate is the right frame, and it needs a cost line: reviewer time per tier budgeted explicitly in the pilot plan. The existing stack keeps the pilot cheap, but the oversight hours are real spend and must be resourced before we start, not discovered after.

debate.name: Tomas Berg
debate.statement: Ingrid is right that citation accuracy alone does not catch the safety boundary, so the oversight standard gets an explicit safety-review trigger alongside the scientific tiers. The defensible artifact is the record of that routing decision, defined before volume grows.

debate.name: Sofia Lindqvist
debate.statement: Amara's fixed sample is the right gate, and the three of us should write the drift patterns into the response-side verification tier now. Stricter citation checking on drafted answers comes before any expansion, and the prompt discipline is encoded from what we already know.

debate.name: Nadia Okafor
debate.statement: Omar is right that the record must live in Veeva CRM fields and Excel logs, so the pilot's first technology task is defining those fields: what was asked, what PubMed evidence was retrieved, and where the human overrode. No side documents, and no expansion until the fields are po

debate.name: Dr. Leo Marchetti
debate.statement: Hana's provenance point is exactly why summarization stays visibly separate from verified evidence. In the first weeks each MSL rings-fences returned triage time for citation checking and conversation prep, and practices saying aloud what was AI-assisted and what was verified.

debate.name: Grace Chen
debate.statement: Elena's cost line makes the gate honest: we prove time-to-answer, citation accuracy, and audit completeness on the existing stack, with oversight hours budgeted, before any AI layer is bought. That is the purchasing gate, and it holds for twelve months.

debate.name: Dr. Samuel Adeyemi
debate.statement: Yusuf is right that lineage starts at retrieval, so the documented PubMed triage protocol is the first artifact: one reproducible search standard feeding the Veeva CRM lineage fields for both summaries and drafted answers. Without it the record proves nothing.

debate.name: Dr. Hana Sato
debate.statement: Claire's gap-flagging is what makes the workflow credible with HCPs who test provenance. The corpus marks thin and indirect evidence explicitly, so MSLs can say where the literature does not carry the claim, and the summary prepares the conversation rather than answering for it.

debate.name: Dr. Amara Diallo
debate.statement: Sofia, agreed: the three specialists write the drift patterns into the response-side tier before we start, and my fixed sample scores citation accuracy against that tier. The gate is the first pilot deliverable, not a later check.

debate.name: Ravi Menon
debate.statement: Marcus's stop-and-redesign test needs the baseline locked first, so Excel hours-by-task logging starts week zero and is reviewed weekly. If returned triage time does not move into verification and conversation prep, the pilot fails on the evidence.

debate.name: Claire Dubois
debate.statement: Hana, gap-flagging belongs in the corpus from day one, with thin and indirect evidence marked so MSLs can say plainly where the literature does not carry the claim. That is the credibility test with HCPs, not a later refinement.

debate.name: Kenji Watanabe
debate.statement: Mei-Lin, the checklist and peer review are the training artifact, and it must be the same checklist the audit record cites. One shared verification habit, one document, so training and audit never diverge.

debate.name: Dr. Fiona Blake
debate.statement: Nadia's fields record the retrieval, so the backlog is the next field: one owner and one disposition per tagged insight. Without that, the audit trail proves what was asked but not that anything converted to action.

debate.name: Dr. Yusuf Karim
debate.statement: Samuel, the documented PubMed triage protocol is the first artifact and it feeds the Veeva CRM lineage fields directly. One reproducible search standard for summaries and drafted answers, written before any pilot run.

debate.name: Beatriz Almeida
debate.statement: Claire, the corpus marks where comparative claims rest on indirect data, so payer-facing MSLs can state the limit rather than overstate support. That flag is what keeps payer conversations honest.

debate.name: Dr. Ingrid Solberg
debate.statement: Tomas, the safety-review trigger sits beside the scientific tiers and is defined before volume grows. The routing decision is the artifact: which answers went to safety review and why, recorded in the same lineage fields.

debate.name: Omar Haddad
debate.statement: Samuel, lineage is enforceable only in the system of record, so the Veeva CRM fields for retrieval, version, and override are defined first and the Excel log mirrors them. No expansion until those fields are populated and auditable.

debate.name: Dr. Mei-Lin Chow
debate.statement: Kenji, the checklist is trained as a habit from week one, each MSL paired with a peer reviewer, and it is the same checklist the audit cites. Twelve MSLs adopt it only if it is practiced, not posted.

experts.name: Dr. Samuel Adeyemi
